newsitem.title: ITALY: Envoy fears more than 80 dead in Albanian shipwreck.
newsitem.headline: Envoy fears more than 80 dead in Albanian shipwreck.

text.p: Tirana's ambassador to Rome said on Sunday that more than 80 Albanians were feared dead following the sinking of a refugee boat off southern Italy.
Pandeli Pasko told Reuters that he had compiled a list of missing people after talking to survivors in the southern Italian port of Brindisi on Saturday.

His figures put the number of people on the boat, which sank on Friday night after colliding with a navy ship trying to head it away from Italy under orders aimed at stemming a tide of illegal immigrants, at between 120 and 130.
Only 34 people were pulled from the water in difficult weather conditions and four bodies, those of three women and one man, were recovered on Friday night.
The Italian navy has said there is no possibility of anyone else having survived but on Saturday it cast doubt on the high estimated death toll given by survivors.
"I spoke to all but two of the survivors individually and they told me who was with them," Pasko said in a telephone interview. "We made up a list as best we could.
"My God, what a tragedy."
A list of names faxed to Reuters by the Albanian embassy referred to 79 missing people, many of them women and children and some identified merely as "a friend".
Pasko said it was not definitive and he had still to speak to two of the survivors.
Two of the missing were identified merely as "a man from Cakrani and his wife" because the survivors did not know them by name but agreed they had been on the boat.
The incident has provoked Tirana's anger and came at a delicate time for Italy, prime mover of the force of police or troops intended to protect food and medical supplies in Albania.
But Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Saturday that the tragedy made the Italian-led mission, authorised by the U.N. Security Council, more urgent.

"We need several days. The operation is complicated, involving taking control of ports in cooperation with regular Albanian forces," Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini told the daily La Stampa newspaper on Sunday.
Dini was asked whether the incident had speeded matters up and raised international sensitivity.
"Absolutely, because illegal immigration is not something that concerns just Italy," he replied.

Italy warned its nationals in southern Albania to limit their stays to the minimum time possible but newspapers quoted Albanian President Sali Berisha as assuring that the Italians would be well received in the country.
Dini told La Stampa that the tragedy was an accident that could not have been easily avoided.
"Our navy had the task of stopping boats bringing illegal immigrants to Italy and the Albanian boat did not stop.
"It tried in every way to evade the two Italian ships and then, after several risky manouevres, set itself on a collision course with our vessel that could not avoid it."
Some of the refugees have been quoted as saying that the Italian ship bore down on them and two enquiries have been opened in Italy to investigate the causes.
Dini said that Italy was not denying anyone's right to asylum but most of the 13,000 Albanians who have flooded into the country in recent weeks were not real refugees.

"What is happening in Albania is the illegal immigration to Italy of people who do not need asylum and who are not seeking asylum. They merely want to cross the borders of the European Union in order to get work," he said.
"Our government's action is right, carefully thought out and balanced. And we have no intention of changing it."
